issues.legal_issue: A settlement deed granting property absolutely subject to terms that reserve a spouse’s lifetime management and enjoyment of other beneficiaries’ shares gives the spouse absolute ownership of the spouse’s own share while limiting the other beneficiaries’ enjoyment during the spouse’s lifetime.
material_facts: A settlement deed granted property to a spouse and two daughters absolutely, subject to terms in the deed.

The deed provided that the spouse would manage and enjoy the properties allocated to the daughters during the spouse’s lifetime, and that the daughters would take those properties absolutely after the spouse’s death.
The deed separately described the spouse and daughters as recipients and used language of absolute ownership elsewhere in the deed.
The dispute in the partition suit concerned whether the spouse’s own share was absolute or only a life interest.
issues.conclusion: The spouse held her one-third share absolutely. The deed reserved to her lifetime management and enjoyment of the daughters’ shares, without giving her ownership of those shares.
issues.legal_principle: The deed must be read as a whole, giving effect to its plain terms. The Court compared the language of the provisions granting property and reserving lifetime enjoyment, including the deed’s use of absolute-ownership language elsewhere. It treated the addition of words about alienation as emphasizing the daughters’ inability to alienate their shares during the spouse’s lifetime, not as restricting the spouse’s ownership of her own share. No statutory provisions or earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.settlement_deed_interpretation_in_partit: The proceeding is a partition suit in which the court must interpret a settlement deed.
predicates.deed_grants_property_absolutely_subject_: The deed grants property absolutely while making the grant subject to stated terms.
predicates.spouse_receives_a_defined_share: The deed grants the spouse a defined share of the property.
predicates.spouse_has_lifetime_management_and_enjoy: The deed gives the spouse management and enjoyment of the other recipients’ shares during the spouse’s lifetime.

issues.definition: When a settlement deed in a partition suit grants property absolutely subject to terms, gives the spouse a defined share, and provides for the spouse’s lifetime management and enjoyment of other shares, the spouse holds the spouse’s own share absolutely and has lifetime enjoyment of those other shares.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary entitled under a settlement deed to manage and enjoy property during the beneficiary’s lifetime is not liable to pay mesne profits for that authorized enjoyment.
material_facts: The deed permitted the spouse to manage and enjoy the properties allocated to the daughters during the spouse’s lifetime.
The spouse remained in possession of those properties under the deed.
The daughters claimed mesne profits, arguing that the spouse held their properties only as a manager and was accountable to them.
The Court construed the deed’s grant of enjoyment as giving the spouse a right to possess the properties and receive their profits during the spouse’s lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The claim for mesne profits was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court interpreted the deed’s terms in context and held that the right to both manage and enjoy the properties entitled the spouse to remain in possession and receive their profits during the spouse’s lifetime. The Court compared this right with the settlor’s own reserved right to possess and enjoy the properties during his lifetime. No statutory provisions or earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.partition_suit_includes_mesne_profits_cl: The proceeding is a partition suit in which a claimant seeks mesne profits.
predicates.occupant_is_authorized_to_manage_and_enj: The deed authorizes the occupant to manage and enjoy the property.
predicates.deed_gives_occupant_lifetime_right_to_en: The deed gives the occupant the right to enjoy the property during the occupant’s lifetime.

issues.definition: When a partition suit includes a mesne-profits claim and the deed authorizes the occupant to manage and enjoy the property for life, mesne profits are not recoverable for that authorized lifetime enjoyment.
